Restating the title, I have the Windows Store version of Halo MCC because it's free if you have an XboxGamePass subscription - I wanted to install a mod for it, but because of the way Windows handles its store's files, you have to change the permissions of... apparently 'volatile,' folders.

Chronologically:

I looked up how to install mods for the Windows Store version of the game.

I went through the process laid out in the Reddit thread I found that showed you how to do it, which, as I said, is as simple as changing permissions on the folders, not a difficult or even really rare thing to do.

When I went to copy out the files you needed to backup for the mod installation, everything broke.

lmfao - E V E R Y T H I N G , broke.

It said Windows couldn't access the 'file' (it was a folder) in an error format I had never seen before.

It was still on my SSD, it was still taking up space, everything was still there, but Windows literally didn't understand what it was anymore.

The folder said it was 0kb large - should be like 32GB or something like that.

The permissions interface didn't have any options to choose anymore and the 'owner' was 'uknown.'

Anyways, I couldn't delete it, rename it, move it, absolutely nothing. It was ~32GB of dead, unchangeable, weight.

Even the Windows App store didn't know what was going on. It wouldn't let me try and reinstall it or anything. It was just flat-out broke and as it stood, it didn't seem as if I would ever be able to do anything with the Halo MCC on my computer ever again.

After searching and searching I finally found a way to fix it and, at time of writing, am currently reinstalling the game.

THE FIX

1. I downloaded and created a bootable drive on a USB drive with Ubuntu (this wasn't hard at all and mostly automated, anyone can do it)

2. Rebooted into Ubuntu and went through the files to find my SSD's storage which also displayed my files from Windows and everything within them.

3. I started deleting all of the folders associated with Halo MCC (which was only 3) and assumed that would fix it, but I wasn't done yet.

4. The game was still elbow deep in my SSD's ass, locked in as if my computer just coofed. I ran CCleaner's registry cleaner in hopes that might help it and since it didn't, I don't know if it would be a required step or not, but I'm just saying all of what I did to fix the issue.

5. Finally, I found a powershell command that would reregister all apps on the Windows Store.

Get-AppXPackage -AllUsers -Name Microsoft.Services.Store* | Foreach {Add-AppxPackage -DisableDevelopmentMode -Register “$($_.InstallLocation)\AppXManifest.xml” -Verbose}

6. After running that it completely expunged the records/registries/whatever that Halo MCC still had locked on my PC.

7. Went back to the game on Windows app store, saw the same - usual interface, clicked install, and gawd dayum it started downloading again.
